name: Protection Mechanism Failure
title: CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure
ai_text: In AI software this weakness shows up as a guard that is missing or applied wrongly. The CVEs sit in LLM application builders, model serving and acceleration libraries, and a chat front end. Langflow lets a crafted component run OS commands on the server. Open WebUI lets crafted URLs slip past its web fetch blocklist. Fickling passes unsafe pickle imports as likely safe. The Intel libraries for PyTorch and TensorFlow, and the oneCCL bindings, let a local user escalate privilege. Attackers reach these through normal product features, such as components, fetched links, or scanned model files, and gain command execution, privilege escalation, or a bypassed filter.
description: The product does not use or incorrectly uses a protection mechanism that provides sufficient defense against directed attacks against the product.
extended_description: This weakness covers three distinct situations. A missing protection mechanism occurs when the application does not define any mechanism against a certain class of attack. An insufficient protection mechanism might provide some defenses - for example, against the most common attacks - but it does not protect against everything that is intended. Finally, an ignored mechanism occurs when a mechanism is available and in active use within the product, but the developer has not applied it in some code path.
